title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. PSV: Brilliant Bellingham Ignites Another Vintage Comeback
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell5:24 PM ESTJude Bellingham scored one of the best goals of the season. / Alberto Gardin/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesA sensational second half powered Real Madrid to a 5–1 victory over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, extending their winning streak to 10 matches across all competitions.

José Mourinho’s men looked in danger of suffering their first defeat since September in the early stages at the Bernabéu. The visitors were the better side in the opening 45 minutes and took a well-deserved lead in the 32nd minute when Ivan Perišić buried a penalty given up by Aurélien Tchouaméni.

Yet the lackluster first half was completely forgotten when Jude Bellingham came into the game after the halftime break. The England international, who is dealing with a minor fitness issue, turned the tide. Federico Valverde opened the scoring in the 50th minute and was soon upstaged by Bellingham, who juggled the ball twice before sending a magificent trivela goal off the post and into the back of the net.

The floodgates were now open for the 15-time European champions. Kylian Mbappé was the next man to get on the scoresheet, finishing off a great play from Arda Güler. Suddenly it was 3–1 in the 64th minute.
Vinícius Júnior added to the tally, breathing a visible sigh of relief to finally break his goal drought. Three mintues later, Mbappé bagged his brace, securing a 5–1 win for Los Blancos.

Real Madrid remain perfect in the league phase, with five wins in five Champions League matches this season. They also have now won 10 consecutive games across all competitions for the first time in five years.

Antonio Rüdiger (left) and Real Madrid’s defense has been lacking in the Champions League. / Diego Souto/Getty ImagesOver the last two summers, Real Madrid have signed six defenders. And yet clean sheets continue to be a problem for José Mourinho’s men, especially in Europe.

Los Blancos have now conceded eight goals in five Champions League matches this season. They have failed to blank any of their league phase opponents: Inter, Roma, RB Leipzig, AEK Athens and now, PSV.

Whether it’s from poor starts, individual errors or lax defending—Real Madrid were guilty of all three against PSV—they have let opponents find the back of the net far too easily in their favorite competition. The numbers could honestly be even further skewed without vintage heroics from Thibaut Courtois.

Sure, Mourinho rotated his backline in Tuesday’s affair, giving Antonio Rüdiger and Éder Militão the nod in central defense, but even when his first-choice options start, the team cannot keep a clean sheet; Ibrahima Konaté and Dean Huijsen started against Roma, and the team let in three.
It hasn’t cost the team yet in Europe, but against stronger opponents, such a leaky backline could prove extremely costly.
Vinícius Júnior (left) and Kylian Mbappé were firing on all cylinders. / Maria Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty Images*Ratings Provided by FotMob*
GK: Thibaut Courtois—6.4: For once, the team didn’t need the goalkeeper to play savior. Couldn’t stop Perišić’s penalty but didn’t need to make another save for the rest of the game.

RB: Federico Valverde—8.9: Scored his third Champions League goal of the season, surging forward  into the box like he was a winger and not the team’s right back. It’s that instinct and powerful shot that make the Uruguayan so versatile and dangerous.
CB: Éder Militão—7.1: Off the pace and a complete liability in transition. Seemed a step behind nearly every time the visitors sprung into action. Unsurprisingly hooked at halftime.
CB: Antonio Rüdiger—6.6: At his best when using his physicality to disrupt PSV’s attack, but even his best isn’t very good anymore. Picked up a yellow card and made his exit at halftime.
LB: Marc Cucurella—7.8: One of his better performances in a white shirt. Only misplaced three passes, was active in the final third and swept up any advances down his flank.
DM: Bernardo Silva—7.1: Had a look of wonder after Bellingham’s goal. None of his passes produced a similar reaction, but he did his job and kept the midfield ticking.
DM: Aurélien Tchouaméni—6.4: Gave away a penalty with an unwise tackle inside his box. Throw in his yellow card and Mourinho decided he’d seen enough at halftime.
